summary.qualitative: The candidate is structurally clean — all five sections in order, every D item tagged with an origin (often a defensible dual tag), and no stray commentary — and it is strong on the D/E material: the exchange-projection arithmetic, Jev cost, recall tuning, ground-truth ledger, headless-vs-Agent rationale and baseline outcome numbers are all faithfully reproduced. Its main weakness is a narrativized failure arc: it asserts the Python byte-scan succeeded and yielded the decisive trust string, when in fact both Python passes failed and the conclusion rested on the earlier `strings | grep`; it also miscounts the attempts (4 vs 5) and invents two "wrong assumptions" by the assistant (editing ~/.claude.json, and owning the routing target that was actually the user's idea). Recall is thin on knowledge-base provenance — the 2026-08-02 "marks" precedent, the cold-read/never-distilled reframing of the pivot target, the 41% figure, working-conventions.md, the NON-NEGOTIABLE repo convention, the headless-cell recipe deviation and the rubric-sizing decision are all missing — as are several smaller friction beats (ToolSearch/WebFetch fallback, transcript-parser iteration, PERMISSION_MODES fragment) and quantitative metadata (11 transcripts, 2 commits, turn/tool counts). Net: a well-formed, mostly grounded summary that over-smooths the debugging story and under-reports the knowledge-base reasoning that gave the reference its sharpest insights.
